newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico corn imports may decline in 1997 - industry. [CORRECTED 23:06 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mexico corn imports may decline in 1997 - industry. [CORRECTED 23:06 GMT]

text.p: Mexico's 1997 corn imports may fall by more than 45 percent from 1996 import levels, the director of the National Animal Feed Manufacturers Association, Fernando Lozano Plascencia, told Reuters.
"This year about 5.7 million tonnes of corn and 1.6 million tonnes of sorghum were imported," Lozano said in an interview.
"For next year, corn imports will probably reach three million or 3.25 million (tonnes). In sorghum, levels should remain around current levels."
Lozano said the estimates are based on official data from the corn- and sorghum-growing sectors and reflect human and animal consumption.
Lower expected imports are due to greater crop production and industry agreements to consume all Mexican grains, Lozano said.
In the first 10 months of the year the animal feed industry consumed 22 percent of imported grains, he added, with total consumption in the industry possibly reaching 13 million tonnes.
